facts.claim: Cancer Council Australia, 'Be SunSmart': 'Sun protection is recommended whenever UV levels reach 3 or higher.' and 'Unlike the sun's heat and light, we can't see or feel UV radiation, so check the UV for your location on the free SunSmart app or on the Bureau of Meteorology website.'
facts.conflicts: Cancer Council Australia is a national health charity (SunSmart program), not a government body. Page is Australian guidance; frame as Australian sun-safety advice, not as a rule for overseas destinations.

facts.claim: Cancer Council Australia, 'Be SunSmart', step 4 Seek shade: 'Use trees, built shade structures, or bring your own (such as a sunshade tent)! Shade reduces UV radiation, but it can still reach you via reflection, so make sure you use shade in combination with other sun protection measures.' The five SunSmart steps are: Slip on covering clothing; Slop on SPF 50 or SPF50+, broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen; Slap on a hat; Seek shade; Slide on some sunglasses.

Cancer Council Australia, 'Be SunSmart': sunscreen should be applied 'at least 20 minutes before you go outside' and reapplied 'every two hours or after swimming or excessive sweating'. 'Remember, sunscreen is not a suit of armour and should be used with other sun protection measures.'

Copied from wedding-centrepieces pack (original fact_02, checked 2026-11-22). South Australian Metropolitan Fire Service, 'Home fire safety fact sheet: Candles': 'A candle is an open flame. It can easily ignite any combustible items nearby.' and 'Keep the immediate area around a candle clear of all items. They should be kept well away from items that can catch fire, such as clothing, books, paper, curtains, Christmas trees and flammable decorations etc.'
facts.conflicts: Fact sheet is written for homes, not venues. Use as general candle-safety guidance; venue open-flame rules are separate (booking checklist).

facts.claim: Copied from wedding-centrepieces pack (original fact_03, checked 2026-11-22). SA MFS candles fact sheet: 'Make sure candles are placed in sturdy holders that will not tip over and place on a secure piece of heat-resistant furniture. Candle holders must be made of material that cannot burn.' and 'Any air movement (draughts) past a candle can cause the candle wax to melt unevenly. The candle may then become unstable and fall over.'
Copied from wedding-centrepieces pack (original fact_04, checked 2026-11-22). SA MFS candles fact sheet: 'Battery operated candles are a good and safe alternative to traditional candles.'

insider_details.detail: Shade alone isn't enough for a daytime garden ceremony: Cancer Council says UV still reaches people by reflection under shade, so pair shaded seating with hats, sunscreen and sunglasses, and check the UV forecast for the location on the day (sun protection is recommended at UV 3 or higher).

Ask the venue what shade exists over the ceremony and drinks lawn (trees or built structures) and whether a sunshade or marquee can be added; a sunscreen station works best set out early, since it goes on at least 20 minutes before guests sit outside.

Evening garden tables and breezes don't mix well with naked flames: the fire service notes draughts make candles burn unevenly and tip, so use sturdy non-combustible holders away from linen and foliage, or battery candles, and ask the venue its open-flame rules.
